status: PREVIEW — the anti-pattern rules from docs/OPTIONS-STRATEGY-V7-ANTIPATTERNS.md, running beside live V7 (Neel, 2026-10-04). Inherits everything from policy_v2.json; only the deliberate differences live here.
differences_from_v7: put_skip_extended = 1 — no new put on a name >= mr_threshold_pct above its 10-day average. Evidence: 95 extended chains paid 0.96%/wk at a 36% assignment rate, against 1.81% / 35% in the normal band and 1.58% / 34% depressed.

roll_abandon_pct = 20 (vol-scaled) — past that gap above the strike, stop citing RSI or the roll credit as a reason to wait; decide on the rule-5 tax test alone. Evidence: 0 of 13 call assignments more than 10% above the strike traded back within 13 weeks ($186,000 given up), against 10 of 18 below 10%.

call_skip_depressed = 1 — no long-term call on a name >= mr_threshold_pct below its 10-day average. Evidence: 174 depressed call chains paid 0.08% of notional against 0.13% normal and 0.29% extended, while the put on the same name in the same week paid 1.58%. The mirror of put_skip_extended.

put_skip_overbought = 1 — no new put on a name at RSI >= put_rsi_unfavourable (65). No put at all rather than a farther one: overbought is the time for calls. Neel, 2026-10-07, on TSM: RSI 69 → a delta-36 put 2% under spot.
put_vol_scale_farther_only = 1 — for puts, volatility scaling may push the delta below its RSI base, never above. The call-side scaling had turned TSM's 'farther' base-20 put into delta 36.

put_skip_lockup = 1 — no new put on a name with a post-IPO lock-up release before the put's expiry + put_lockup_window_days (7). Dates in data/lockup_calendar.json. Neel, 2026-10-12, on CBRS at $147: 19.4M shares unlocking 10/14, more 10/28 and 11/9.

st_call_skip_depressed = 1 — call_skip_depressed extended to the short-term book: no new call on a name >= mr_threshold_pct below its 10-day average. Same evidence (0.08% yield on depressed calls), plus the shares there often just came by assignment and a call at the bottom can sell them below cost. Neel, 2026-10-12.

call_roll_up = 1 — a call roll takes the highest strike a week out that still pays a net credit (call_roll_min_credit_ps), not only the same strike; a near-the-money call (delta ≥ call_roll_up_min_delta) is flagged any day a free lift of ≥ call_roll_up_min_lift_pct is there. Evidence: AMD $545 → $560 10/30 for $0.02 on 2026-10-16 after AMD fell 10%; V7 showed nothing.

call_roll_deep_out = 1 — a call ≥ call_roll_deep_itm_pct in the money, above its strike for ≥ call_roll_deep_min_weeks (4) straight weeks, RSI under assign_rsi, rolls to the soonest expiry up to call_roll_max_weeks (13) where a credit roll puts the strike within call_roll_near_spot_pct (2%) of the stock. Evidence: AAPL $325 → $340 Jan 15 for $0.85 on 2026-10-16, above $325 every day since 9/10; the weekly roll only kept $325. Not for a one-week spike: AVGO crossed $375 on 10/6 and was $337 a week later, weekly calls expired at $0.01.
